_comment: The committed floor for the RETRIEVAL suite. mvn verify fails below it.
These numbers are LOW compared to a live run, and the reason is worth stating
precisely rather than waved at: LlmStub.returnsEmbedding() returns the SAME 768-
dimension vector for every query and every chunk, because a stub cannot compute a
real embedding. Cosine distance between identical vectors is a constant zero, so the
vector CTE's ORDER BY has no signal to sort on and returns an essentially arbitrary
50 chunks out of the tenant's ~150. Those 50 then contribute a real RRF score
(1/(60+rank)) to chunks that were never actually similar to the query.
That is not merely 'no help' -- it actively competes with the lexical signal. A
genuinely relevant chunk ranked 1st lexically scores ~0.0164 from that alone; an
unrelated chunk that happened to land at vector rank 1 by tie-break order scores the
same ~0.0164 from pure noise, and can equal or outrank the real match. Measured on
the full 75-document corpus against these 70 cases: overall Recall@5 ≈ 0.23, MRR ≈
0.17 -- including on the IDENTIFIER group, where lexical matching alone should score
far higher and does not, because the noisy vector half is dragging genuinely-correct
lexical top hits down in the fused ranking.
This is a real property of RRF worth knowing rather than a bug to route around: rank
fusion assumes both signals are informative, and when one is pure noise, fusion can
score worse than either input alone would. It is also exactly why this suite has to
exist and be run against a live model before the retrieval design is trusted -- a
CI number this low would be alarming if read as the system's real quality, so the
floor is set to catch an actual regression (a broken query, a dropped tenant filter,
recall collapsing to zero) rather than to represent expected production quality.
The number worth quoting in the README is a LIVE run's, dated, with the Task 11
lexical-vs-vector-vs-hybrid comparison table run against real embeddings.
